clue.text: Attendant set out with care

indicators.note: set out suggests these three letters are laid out afresh in a new order

parts.note: a child in care is a ward of the court or council, so care gives this word

explanation.surface: A servant arranges something thoughtfully.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges SET into STE. A ward is someone placed in another's care.
explanation.definitionFit: A steward is a ship or aircraft attendant who looks after passengers.

clue.text: Giant rat's home is a problem before middle of boat-race

parts.note: a sum is an arithmetic problem

indicators.note: middle of takes the central letters of the hyphenated word, dropping its outer pairs

explanation.surface: Where a monstrous rodent lives, linked to a rowing contest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'middle of boat-race' gives ATRA, the central four letters. The giant rat of Sumatra is a story Sherlock Holmes mentions but never tells.
explanation.definitionFit: Conan Doyle's Holmes alludes to the Giant Rat of Sumatra, an untold case, placing that rodent on the Indonesian island.

clue.text: It grows down as it grows up

definitions.text: It grows down as it grows up

parts.words: It grows down as it grows up
parts.note: a sea duck that produces soft feathers while it matures

explanation.surface: A paradox about something shrinking as it gets bigger.
explanation.walkthrough: 'down' looks like the opposite of 'up', but it is soft feathering, and growing up means maturing.
explanation.definitionFit: The eider is a sea duck famed for the soft breast feathers used to fill quilts.

clue.text: Titan carrying collection of books — one is "the lost continent"

indicators.note: carrying means holding inside, so the other pieces go within this one

parts.note: Atlas was the Titan who held up the heavens
NT is the New Testament, a collection of books of the Bible
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A giant holding up a library, with one volume about a vanished land.
explanation.walkthrough: 'carrying' puts NT and I inside ATLAS.
explanation.definitionFit: Atlantis is the legendary island civilisation said by Plato to have sunk beneath the sea.

clue.text: Sissy has swim round river

indicators.note: round means surrounding, so one piece goes around the other

parts.note: a dip is a short swim

explanation.surface: A timid person goes swimming around a river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'round' puts DIP around R.
explanation.definitionFit: A drip is a feeble, wet, ineffectual person, much like a wimp.

clue.text: Red skirts carried by prisoner

indicators.note: carried by means held within, so one word goes inside the other

parts.note: a con is a convict, a prisoner
skirts as edges or borders means rims

explanation.surface: Red skirts smuggled out by an inmate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'carried by' puts RIMS inside CON. 'Skirts' looks like clothing but means edges.
explanation.definitionFit: Crimson is a deep shade of red.

clue.text: Dispute French version of tale about jet

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the tale wraps the colour word

parts.note: conte is the French word for a tale or short story
jet as a glossy black colour, like raven, which also means black

explanation.surface: Arguing over a French retelling of a story about an aircraft.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts RAVEN inside CONTE. 'jet' seems to be an aircraft but is the black colour.
explanation.definitionFit: To contravene a statement is to deny or contradict it, a sense of dispute.

clue.text: Completely useless if only half of it is included

definitions.text: Completely useless if only half of it is included

parts.words: Completely useless if only half of it is included
parts.note: describes a phrase meaning entirely, as with a payment that is worthless unless the whole sum is handed over

explanation.surface: A warning that a half-measure is worthless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Completely' is the definition; the rest hints that something paid or quoted this way must not be cut by half.
explanation.definitionFit: In full means entirely, with nothing omitted, so it matches completely.

clue.text: Hints of honey and lime in Spanish punch is Hilton's creation

annotationWithheld.why: Hints of honey and lime in Spanish punch is Hilton's creation: H and L go separately into SANGRIA (S-H-ANGRI-L-A); a single container with the two first letters as its inner piece validates in --try but crashes annotate_check's view (StopIteration on a split insert), and the nested form is refused as nestedSameOp
annotationWithheld.clue: Hints of honey and lime in Spanish punch is Hilton's creation

clue.text: At end of season Surrey constructed facility for development

indicators.note: at end of picks the final letter of the word that follows
constructed means built up from parts, so these letters are reassembled

explanation.surface: A cricket county builds a training ground once the season ends.
explanation.walkthrough: 'At end of season' gives N; 'constructed' rearranges SURREY into URSERY. Surrey is an English county with a cricket team.
explanation.definitionFit: A nursery is a place where young plants or children are reared, and figuratively a breeding ground for talent.

clue.text: Cook laid lemon round piece of meat

indicators.note: to cook something up is to concoct it, so these words are reworked into a new order

explanation.surface: A recipe instruction: arrange lemon slices around the meat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cook' rearranges LAID and LEMON. 'round' belongs to the definition, not the recipe.
explanation.definitionFit: A medallion is a small round cut of meat, typically beef or pork.

clue.text: Taste tiniest amount of laksa during carnival

indicators.note: during means inside the span of, so one piece sits within the other

parts.note: a fair is a carnival or funfair

indicators.note: the tiniest amount of a word is its opening letter alone

explanation.surface: Sampling a little Malaysian noodle soup at a festival.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tiniest amount of laksa' is L, set inside FAIR by 'during'. Laksa is a spicy Malaysian noodle soup.
explanation.definitionFit: Flair can mean stylish discernment, a good eye for style, which is one sense of taste.

clue.text: Chap in the toilet

indicators.note: in tells us one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: Ron is a man's name, any chap

explanation.surface: A man found in the lavatory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts RON inside THE. The informal name for a toilet as a seat of power is the joke.
explanation.definitionFit: Throne is a jocular colloquial word for a lavatory seat.

clue.text: Penny left old vagrant without introduction

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so one piece wraps the other

parts.note: rogue in its old sense is a wandering vagrant

explanation.surface: A small coin left by an old tramp who goes without.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' means outside here: ROGUE goes round LO. 'without introduction' looks like a deletion signal, but 'introduction' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A prologue is the opening section that introduces a play or book.

clue.text: Being after money directors make cuts here!

indicators.note: after places the directors following the money in the answer

parts.note: bread is slang for money
a company's board is its body of directors

explanation.surface: A jibe that money-hungry executives decide on the job cuts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after' sets BOARD behind BREAD. 'Being after money' paints greedy executives; 'cuts' are slices, not redundancies.
explanation.definitionFit: A wooden board on which loaves are sliced is where the knife does its cutting.

clue.text: Type of frame seen in collection of art in public record office?

indicators.note: in places the jumbled letters inside the other word

parts.note: an archive is a place where public records are kept

indicators.note: a collection of letters gathered together in any order, so these are rearranged

explanation.surface: Asking what kind of frame an art collection gets in a records office.
explanation.walkthrough: 'collection of art' rearranges ART into TRA, and 'in' sets it inside ARCHIVE.
explanation.definitionFit: An architrave is the moulded frame surrounding a door or window.

clue.text: Mind short people in the pink

indicators.note: short means cut off before the end, so the closing letter goes

parts.note: to mind something is to care about it
a nation is a people

explanation.surface: Looking after short people who are in good health.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short' trims CARE to CAR. 'in the pink' reads as the idiom for healthy, but 'in' is a link and 'the pink' is the flower.
explanation.definitionFit: Pinks are the Dianthus flower genus, to which the garden carnation belongs.

clue.text: Large order

explanation.surface: A two-word note about a big sequence.
explanation.definitionFit: A tidy sum is a large one; to tidy a room is to put it in order.

clue.text: General store, say, to which I take bag

parts.note: a mart is a market or store
to net is to bag or catch

explanation.surface: Someone visits a general store and takes a bag.
explanation.walkthrough: 'General store' looks like a shop; split it: General is the definition, store gives MART.
explanation.definitionFit: Jean Martinet was a strict 17th-century French army officer whose name now means a disciplinarian.

clue.text: Blades decapitate pigs

indicators.note: decapitate means take off the head, the opening letter of the word

parts.note: boars are male or wild pigs

explanation.surface: A grim instruction to behead swine with knives.
explanation.walkthrough: 'decapitate' removes the B of BOARS. 'Blades' is not knives but the flat ends of oars.
explanation.definitionFit: Oars are named for their blades, the flat parts that push the water, so blades stands for them.

clue.text: Curious delivery gets you 20

definitions.note: refers to the entry at 20-down, meaning peculiar

parts.note: curious means odd
a ball is a delivery from a bowler in cricket

explanation.surface: An unusual bowl in cricket earns twenty runs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'delivery' is a bowled ball in cricket. The number points to the clue at 20-down, whose answer is a synonym.
explanation.definitionFit: Oddball as an adjective means eccentric or peculiar.

clue.text: After sweet she's nothing at all!

definitions.text: After sweet she's nothing at all!

parts.words: After sweet she's nothing at all
parts.note: the woman whose name follows 'sweet' in a slang phrase meaning nothing whatever

explanation.surface: A dismissive remark about a woman once her sweetness is gone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sweet' looks like a dessert or a description of her, but it is the word that comes before her name in the British expression meaning absolutely nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: Sweet Fanny Adams is British slang for nothing whatever, from a Victorian murder victim's name.

clue.text: Different way to go over mountains

indicators.note: in a down entry, going over means sitting above, so this piece comes first

parts.note: ST is the abbreviation for street, a way
a range is a chain of mountains

explanation.surface: A new route that crosses the hills.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to go over' puts ST above RANGE in the down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Strange means unfamiliar or unusual, so other than the norm.

clue.text: Three Russian officials keep Israeli PM away from Gorbachev's policy

indicators.note: keep together with away from tells us to remove one piece from the other
away from completes the instruction to take the prime minister out of the policy

parts.note: perestroika was Gorbachev's programme of restructuring the Soviet system
Shimon Peres was an Israeli prime minister

explanation.surface: Russian leaders keep an Israeli politician out of Soviet reforms.
explanation.walkthrough: 'keep ... away from' removes PERES from PERESTROIKA.
explanation.definitionFit: A troika is a ruling group of three, especially in Soviet politics.

clue.text: Long pompous speech — a bride's unhappy with it

indicators.note: unhappy suggests the letters are disturbed and put into a new order

parts.note: bride's reads as bride is, so the word bride alone is fodder

explanation.surface: A bride complains bitterly about a long-winded wedding speech.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unhappy' rearranges A, BRIDE and IT; the 's is 'is', a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A diatribe is a lengthy bitter tirade, a ranting harangue.

clue.text: One tends to fire author of scary stories

explanation.surface: Describing a storyteller by the fireside.
explanation.definitionFit: A stoker feeds a furnace; Bram Stoker wrote the horror novel Dracula.

clue.text: Old sailor in his boat upset losing a bit of hard cash

indicators.note: upset in a down entry means turned upside down, so the letters run backwards
losing means some letters drop out of the assembled word
in places the sailor inside his boat

parts.note: the ark was Noah's boat
Noah, the biblical patriarch who sailed the ark

indicators.note: a bit of a word is its opening letter

explanation.surface: An ancient mariner capsizes and loses his money.
explanation.walkthrough: NOAH in ARK gives ANOAHRK; 'losing a bit of hard' removes A and H for ANORK; 'upset' turns it up.
explanation.definitionFit: The krona is the currency of Sweden and the krona of Iceland, so a form of cash.

clue.text: Some porn and marketing primarily?

indicators.note: primarily means at first, so the opening letters of each word are taken

explanation.surface: Asking whether junk mail is mostly smut and adverts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'primarily' takes the first letters; the whole clue also describes junk email.
explanation.definitionFit: Spam is unsolicited bulk email, much of it advertising or explicit content.

clue.text: You were somewhere else? What kind of excuse is that!

definitions.text: You were somewhere else? What kind of excuse is that!

parts.words: You were somewhere else? What kind of excuse is that
parts.note: an incredulous retort that names the type of defence which claims absence from the scene

explanation.surface: A sceptical parent or detective scoffing at a claim of being elsewhere.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as a scoff, but taken literally it asks which defence rests on being somewhere else.
explanation.definitionFit: An alibi is a plea that one was elsewhere when the crime was committed.

clue.text: Instrument al gore keeps to compose

indicators.note: keeps means holds inside, so one piece is wrapped around the other

parts.note: the name Al taken as written
to gore is to pierce with a horn, so horn can mean gore as a verb
to pen a letter is to compose it

explanation.surface: A former US vice-president keeps writing music.
explanation.walkthrough: Al Gore is the former US vice-president, but split up: AL plus HORN ('gore') keeps PEN ('compose').
explanation.definitionFit: An alpenhorn is a very long wooden horn played by Alpine herders, a musical instrument.

clue.text: Inside fat there's some cord

indicators.note: inside places one piece within the other

parts.note: lard is pig fat
any can mean some, as in have you any bread

explanation.surface: String found inside a lump of fat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Inside' puts ANY in LARD; 'fat' is the noun, not an adjective describing the cord.
explanation.definitionFit: A lanyard is a cord worn round the neck to carry a whistle or pass.

clue.text: Get fuel to distribute round river in china

indicators.note: round means surrounding, so one piece wraps the other

parts.note: to mete out is to distribute or allot
the Han is a river in China, a tributary of the Yangtze

explanation.surface: Shipping fuel around a waterway in Asia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'round' puts HAN inside METE. Lowercase 'china' suggests porcelain or the rhyming-slang mate, but it is the country.
explanation.definitionFit: Methane is the main component of natural gas, burnt as fuel.
